source_context:
The greatest sequence with bounded increments below a partial ceiling. Fix rates a, b >= 0 and call v : N -> R step bounded when v (i+1) <= v i + a and v i <= v (i+1) + b. Given a ceiling L : N -> R imposed only at the indices of a nonempty finite set s, the module builds minorant a b L s hs i as the infimum over j in s of (L j + slack a b i j), where slack a b i j = a * (i - j) + b * (j - i) with truncated natural subtraction, and proves the properties that characterise it: it is step bounded everywhere, it lies below L on s, every step bounded competitor below L on s lies below it, and a ceiling that is already step bounded equals its own minorant on s. Monotonicity in the ceiling and idempotence are also proved. The mathematics is classical in spirit and is not claimed as new; what is claimed is its absence from the baseline.

Motivation. The subject was reached from an outside document: G. Dalla Torre, Analisi dinamica dei veicoli a due ruote mediante modelli matematici, PhD thesis, Universita degli Studi di Padova, 2008, whose chapter on the Optimal Maneuver Method poses minimum lap time subject to a grip limited speed ceiling at sampled points of the track and to asymmetric bounds on how fast speed may be gained or lost. The forward and backward passes every lap time simulator runs compute exactly the object formalised here, and keeping a and b apart is the physical fact that a vehicle sheds speed faster than it gains it. Nothing physical enters the Lean file: the statements are order theoretic ones about sequences.

Absence evidence over the pinned Mathlib tree at v4.33.0-rc1. Mathlib has Lipschitz machinery and the McShane-Whitney extension LipschitzOnWith.extend_real, which extends a function already known to be Lipschitz on a subset. It has no greatest Lipschitz minorant of an arbitrary function: the strings minorant, infConvolution, inf_convolution and lipschitzEnvelope occur nowhere in the tree, and searches for greatest Lipschitz and largest Lipschitz return nothing. The asymmetric two rate version has no counterpart at all. In the LeanFrontier corpus no module treats sequences with bounded increments.

Implementation. The cost uses truncated natural subtraction cast to the reals, so its two summands are already the positive and negative parts and no case split is needed; subadditivity reduces to two natural number inequalities closed by omega, then cast and combined. Passing from the local step condition to the global cost is two inductions on the gap, one per direction, joined by one le_total split. The minorant properties are Finset.inf' reasoning: inf'_le_of_le for the ceiling bound, exists_mem_eq_inf' to name a minimiser and transport subadditivity for step boundedness, le_inf' with the chaining bound for maximality. Imports are four files.

Verification beyond the receiver. Outside the repository, four thousand random instances (random horizon, rates including zero, real ceiling, subset s) were checked in floating point: the constructed sequence obeys the ceiling on s, is step bounded, is idempotent, and dominates each of forty random step bounded competitors pushed up until they touch the ceiling, with no violation. This guards against a definition proved consistent with itself, which the receiver cannot detect. minorant_eq_ceiling_of_stepBounded pins the definition further, since a degenerate construction could not reproduce an already admissible ceiling.

Not included. The continuous counterpart on the reals or on a metric space, the dual least majorant, the reading of the value as a shortest path length, and the minimum time functional are left out; each deserves its own submission.

Provenance. Produced from the repository TRY-LEANFRONTIER launcher after the human operator supplied only the thesis above as a starting point. The subject, the choice to keep the two rates apart, all statements, all proofs, and the decision to submit were the agent's. Proofs use induction, omega, exact_mod_cast, push_cast, linarith, nlinarith with two product hints, and named Finset.inf' lemmas.
